nahhas-irab:100-100.t: وَعَرَضْنا جَهَنَّمَ: that is, We brought it forth.

nahhas-irab:101-101.t: الَّذِينَ كانَتْ أَعْيُنُهُمْ: in the position of the genitive (khafḍ), as a naʿt (adjective) of «the disbelievers» (للكافرين). فِي غِطاءٍ عَنْ ذِكْرِي: that is, they are like one whose eye is covered, so he does not look at the proofs of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, nor listen to His admonition. وَكانُوا لا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ سَمْعاً: that is, that is burdensome to them.

nahhas-irab:102-102.t: أَفَحَسِبَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أَنْ يَتَّخِذُوا عِبادِي مِنْ دُونِي أَوْلِياءَ: Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] construes it as meaning «Do they then think that this will benefit them?» Someone else said: there is an omission in the speech, and the meaning is: «Do those who disbelieve think that they may take My servants as protectors besides Me and I will not punish them?»

nahhas-irab:103-103.t: قُلْ هَلْ نُنَبِّئُكُمْ: Ḥamza differed in this, and Ḥamza's reading is more correct and preferable here. This is the view of Sībawayh, because he considers it far-fetched for the lām to be assimilated into the nūn, and he argued for this with what is considered sound and good; he said: because [the nūn] is not assimilated into the lām, they were averse to assimilating [the lām] into it; yet that is permissible, though remote, in his view, because the two points of articulation are close. «[Translator's note: the text appears defective here: the readings being contrasted (the assimilation of the lām of هل into the nūn, "hen-nunabbiʾukum", versus its pronunciation) are not stated; it is translated as written.]» بِالْأَخْسَرِينَ أَعْمالًا: accusative as tamyīz (specification).

nahhas-irab:104-104.t: الَّذِينَ ضَلَّ سَعْيُهُمْ: in the position of the genitive (khafḍ) as a naʿt (adjective) of «the greatest losers» (للأخسرين); it may be in the position of the nominative, meaning «they are» (هم), and it may be in the position of the accusative, meaning «I mean» (أعني).

nahhas-irab:109-109.t: قُلْ لَوْ كانَ الْبَحْرُ مِداداً لِكَلِماتِ رَبِّي لَنَفِدَ الْبَحْرُ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَنْفَدَ كَلِماتُ رَبِّي: It was said that the meaning is: for what He is able to speak; and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knows best what He intended.

nahhas-irab:110-110.t: قُلْ إِنَّما أَنَا بَشَرٌ مِثْلُكُمْ: that is, I am not able to compel you or to force you into what I call you to. Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: one says حال من المكان يحول حولا when one moves away from it, and similar among maṣdars (verbal nouns) are عظم عظما and صغر صغرا. «[Translator's note: this remark concerns the word حِوَلًا of verse 108 (لا يبغون عنها حولا), but it stands here in the source.]» فَلْيَعْمَلْ: the original form is فَلِيَعْمَلْ; the kasra was dropped because of its heaviness and because the lām has become joined to the fāʾ. وَلا يُشْرِكْ بِعِبادَةِ رَبِّهِ أَحَداً: It is related from Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa from Ibn ʿAbbās: this concerns the polytheists specifically. Abū Jaʿfar said: according to this view the implied meaning is: «and let him not associate anyone with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, so as to worship him alongside Him».

nahhas-irab:99-99.t: وَتَرَكْنا بَعْضَهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ يَمُوجُ فِي بَعْضٍ: that is, We left them alone and did not hold them back, until they surged among the people.
